referencePolicy.officialSc2Portrait: Temporary Blizzard-hosted visual reference for factual pilot anatomy and equipment only; not copied into the repository or redistributed.
referencePolicy.classicLocalPortrait: Existing development-internal portrait used only for cramped cockpit framing and SC1 communication ambience.
referencePolicy.originality: All deliverables are newly rendered 2D assets; no source image is included in a deliverable.

idlePrompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original game communication portrait keyframe, square 1:1, readable at 96 px. Input images: Image 1 is an official Blizzard StarCraft II Goliath portrait used only as factual character-equipment and anatomy reference; Image 2 is the locally held classic StarCraft communication portrait used only for cramped cockpit framing, analog green scan ambience, and strong close-up readability. Do not copy either image pixel-for-pixel and do not reproduce their exact pose or composition. Primary request: create a newly rendered, legally distributable 2D painted cinematic portrait of the same recognizable Goliath pilot archetype, reconciling the SC2 pilot construction with the SC1 communications mood. Subject invariants: adult Black male human walker pilot; broad but natural human face; clean shaved scalp; short neat moustache and compact goatee; two large rounded amber-orange tinted goggles with visible human eyes behind them; dark segmented cranial interface plates running over the crown and temples; round ear-interface housings with thin orange luminous rings; exposed nose, cheeks, mouth and jaw; thick dark navy neck seal; symmetrical heavy dark blue-gray cockpit shoulder restraints and chest harness with small amber indicators. The headgear is an open neural/optical rig, not a sealed helmet, gas mask, robot skull, Marine helmet, Thor cockpit, or respirator. Scene/backdrop: enclosed Goliath walker cockpit, close structural rails and two dim side screens, no exterior mech visible. Composition/framing: frontal neutral idle, head and upper chest fill about 72% of square; shoulders fully present and anatomically connected, enough safe margin for circular crop; level camera and level shoulders. Style/medium: original hand-painted 2D science-fiction game portrait, disciplined military industrial realism, crisp silhouette and large readable shapes, subtly evocative of late-1990s RTS comms upgraded with modern SC2 material modeling; not anime, not glossy AI concept art, not photoreal screenshot. Lighting/mood: dark olive/teal cockpit ambient light, restrained amber practical lights on goggles and harness, skin remains naturally readable; no dramatic colored relighting. Constraints: one portrait only; no text, logos, UI frame, watermark, weapons, wounds, scars, blood, smoke, sparks, cracks, grime changes, or facial asymmetry. The exact face, goggle geometry, cranial plates, earpieces, shoulder restraints, chest harness, camera, crop, palette, and cockpit layout will be the immutable identity anchor for later state keyframes. Avoid: sealed mask; fully enclosed helmet; robotic face; glowing blue eyes; tiny head inside a mech chest; oversized shoulders that cut off anatomy; cropped shoulders; extra lenses; missing ear device; facial injury; exaggerated grimace; animation sheet or collage.
editBase: Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: one square Goliath pilot communication state keyframe. Image 1 is the exact approved identity anchor and edit target. Preserve exactly the adult Black male face, scalp, moustache, compact goatee, skin tone, eyes, rounded amber goggles, dark crown and temple interface plates, orange circuit lines, circular earpieces, neck seal, blue-gray shoulder restraints, chest harness, wear pattern, colors, camera, crop, lighting and cockpit geometry. Both shoulders remain fully visible and anatomically connected. Change only the requested physical pose. One image only; no text, UI, border, logo, watermark, weapon, wound, scar, blood, crack, sparks, smoke or new object. Do not turn the subject into a sealed helmet, respirator or robot face. These are state-switch keyframes, not a continuous animation.

states.prompt: Turn the head about 16 degrees toward viewer-right, lift the chin about 4 degrees, and shift the eyes toward the right cockpit display before returning attention to the interlocutor. Rotate the shoulders only about 3 degrees inside fixed restraints. Preserve believable near/far perspective in the goggle rims and earpieces; keep the cockpit and camera stationary. Motion must read at 96 px through pose rather than glow.

Pitch the head downward about 11 degrees and translate it slightly forward. Aim the eyes forward and upward through the same lenses toward the targeting field, firm the closed jaw, brace both shoulders upward and inward against the restraints, and show tension in the chest harness. Fixed camera and cockpit; no muzzle flash or weapon.

Show a sudden non-injuring impact reaction: torso remains caught by the harness, head recoils slightly backward and rolls about 13 degrees toward viewer-left with a small 6-degree left turn, viewer-left shoulder rises and viewer-right shoulder drops, eyes glance toward a side instrument, and mouth remains closed. This is a pose reaction only; all equipment remains intact and there is no cosmetic damage.
